learning_outcomes.text: Demonstrate possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, typically at a level supported by advanced textbooks but also including aspects derived from the forefront of the field.

Know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
Have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Be able to transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Choose and apply the most suitable methods and techniques to analyze and solve problems defined by data that represent a challenge due to their volume, velocity, variety, or heterogeneity, including computational, mathematical, statistical, and signal processing methods.

Have the experimental and analytical skills to work autonomously, being able to propose experiments and to describe, analyze, evaluate, and interpret the resulting information to propose alternative and novel solutions to known and/or emerging problems.
Create models and make decisions based on available data, combining acquired knowledge and being able to apply new knowledge to problem-solving.
Ability to integrate into a multidisciplinary team within the framework of a data science project.
Ability to express data processing results clearly and convincingly, both in writing and orally.
Analyze data from complex phenomena by applying statistical techniques and probability calculus.
Understand and correctly apply exploratory data analysis and statistical modeling techniques, evaluating model quality, validating them, and interpreting them.
Know and apply the main Descriptive Statistics techniques, determining the most appropriate for each dataset based on its characteristics.
Know the main data collection techniques and the most common errors in a sampling process.
Apply punctual estimation techniques for unknown parameters from a sample, and determine the error associated with the estimation.
Construct confidence intervals for the main parameters of interest in the context of data analysis, and determine the minimum sample size to bound the error committed with a given confidence level.
Fluently handle the concepts of statistic, critical region, significance level, and p-value.
Be able to test hypotheses about proportions and means, both with independent and paired samples, determining the ideal type of test for each situation.

syllabus_topics: Statistical data summary: frequency tables, graphical representations, summary measures.
Data collection techniques. Introduction to statistical inference.
Confidence intervals. Confidence level and error bounds. Sample sizes.
Introduction to hypothesis testing. Significance level, critical region, and p-value.

Examples of hypothesis tests. Proportions: comparison of one or several proportions. Normal populations: comparison of one or several populations. Paired samples and independent samples. ANOVA and ANCOVA.
teaching_methods: Laboratory practical classes (on-site) using R language

assessment_methods.method: Attendance, participation in seminars and tutorials (including online)
Active participation in forums and/or Campus Virtual activities (exercises, assignments)
Reports, memoirs, and/or practical exams (computer practical sessions)
Final exam (written test with practical exercises and theoretical questions)

assessment_rules: The final grade in the ordinary call is calculated as 0.05 x PA + 0.15 x AC + 0.2 x PL + 0.6 x EX, where PA is participation, AC is active participation in forums, PL is practical exams, and EX is the final exam. No minimum grade is required for individual elements. The final grade must be at least 5 out of 10 to pass the course. In the extraordinary call, students may retake the practical exam and the final exam; taking these exams implicitly waives the corresponding grade from the ordinary call. For differentiated evaluation, the procedure is an 80% theoretical-practical exam and a 20% laboratory test.
